name: portless
description: Replace port numbers with stable, named local URLs. For humans and agents.
readmeExcerpt:
# portless Replace port numbers with stable, named .localhost URLs for local development. For humans and agents.

```diff - "dev": "next dev" # http://localhost:3000 + "dev": "portless run next dev" # https://myapp.localhost ``` portless runs a local reverse proxy and gives each dev server a name. Your app listens on a free port that portless assigns, and you open `https://.localhost` instead of remembering which port it took. The URL stays the same across restarts, so bookmarks, cookies, OAuth redirects, and an agent's test script keep pointing at the right app. ## Install ```bash npm install -g portless ``` To pin the version per project, install it as a dev dependency with `npm install -D portless`. portless is pre-1.0, so contributors may run different versions, and a change to the state directory format between releases can require running `portless trust` again. ## Quick start From a project with a `"dev"` script in `package.json`: ```bash portless # -> runs "dev", https://.localhost ``` The name comes from `package.json`, the git root, or the directory. Pass a name and a command to choose both: ```bash portless myapp next dev # -> https://myapp.localhost ``` - The proxy starts on the first run. It serves HTTPS with HTTP/2 on port 443, so the first run creates a local certificate authority, adds it to the system trust store, and may ask for `sudo`. Use `--no-tls` for plain HTTP, or `--unprivileged` to skip `sudo` ([Unprivileged mode](https://portless.sh/commands#unprivileged-mode)). - `portless run ` infers the name and detects git worktrees. In a linked worktree, the last `/` segment of the branch becomes a subdomain, so `fix-ui.myapp.localhost` and `myapp.localhost` run side by side. Use `--prefix` or `PORTLESS_PREFIX` to set the label, or [configure the label style and hostname template](https://portless.sh/configuration#worktree-hostnames). - A name with dots is a subdomain: `portless api.myapp pnpm start` serves `https://api.myapp.localhost`. - `PORTLESS=0 pnpm dev` runs the command directly, without the proxy. The full walkthrough is in [Getting started](https://portless.sh). ## How it works Each app gets a random port from 4000 to 4999 through the `PORT` environment variable, and registers a route from its hostname to that port. The proxy forwards `https://.localhost` to the route. Most frameworks read `PORT`. For those that don't, such as Vite, Astro, Angular, Expo, and Wrangler, portless adds the matching port and host flags to the command ([Port assignment](https://portless.sh/configuration#port-assignment)). Outside LAN mode, the proxy listens only on `127.0.0.1` and `::1`. It keeps `/etc/hosts` in sync for route hostnames, which custom TLDs such as `.test` need. If a route hostname will not resolve, the command that registered it warns and points you to `portless hosts sync`. To reach an app from another device or share it, use [LAN mode](https://portless.sh/commands#lan-mode) for phones on the same network, or [Tailscale](https://portless.sh/commands#share-on-tailscale), [ngrok](https://portless.sh/commands#share-with-ngrok), or a [Cloudflare quick tunnel](https://portless.sh/commands#share-with-cloudflare) with `--tailscale`, `--ngrok`, or `--cloudflare`. ### Upstream aliases Use `--upstream` to route an alias to an HTTP or HTTPS service listening on loopback: ```bash portless alias api 8080 --upstream https portless alias api 8080 --upstream https://api.internal portless alias api 8080 --upstream http://api.internal ``` The positional port always dials loopback. `https` enables TLS and preserves the incoming Host header. An `https://` authority enables TLS and overrides Host with the full authority, including its optional port. SNI uses a DNS hostname without the port; IP addresses are not sent as SNI. An `http://` authority overrides Host without TLS. This setting does not change client-facing proxy TLS. Authorities accept only a hostname or IP address with an optional port, without credentials, paths, queries, fragments, or whitespace. Upstream TLS connects only to an HTTP/1.1 backend on loopback. Portless disables certificate verification, so TLS does not authenticate backend identity, even through an SSH tunnel. Restart the proxy daemon after upgrading portless. ## Configuration An optional `portless.json` sets the name and script. In a monorepo, one file at the root covers every workspace package, and `portless` from the root starts all of them: ```json { "apps": { "apps/web": { "name": "myapp" }, "apps/api": { "name": "api.myapp" } } } ``` A `"portless"` key in `package.json` works too. Fields, precedence, Turborepo setup, and environment variables are in [Configuration](https://portless.sh/configuration). ## For AI agents Install the portless skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/portless): ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/portless ``` For MCP clients, `portless mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio. The default `core` profile lists routes, looks up URLs, and manages static aliases. `--tools all` adds proxy control and diagnostics: ```json { "mcpServers": { "portless": { "command": "portless", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` The server does not start dev servers. Agents run `portless run ` in a shell. See [MCP server](https://portless.sh/commands#mcp-server). ## Commands Run `portless --help` for the full list, or `portless --help` for one command. | Group | Commands | Docs | | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Run apps | `portless`, `run`, ` `, `get` | [Run an app](https://portless.sh/commands#run-an-app), [Get a service URL](https://portless.sh/commands#get-a-service-url) | | Static routes | `alias`, `compose up`, `compose down` | [Alias](https://portless.sh/commands#alias-static-routes), [Docker Compose](https://portless.sh/commands#docker-compose) | | Proxy | `proxy start`, `proxy stop`, `service install`, `service status`, `service uninstall` | [Proxy control](https://portless.sh/commands#proxy-control), [OS startup service](https://portless.sh/commands#os-startup-service) | | HTTPS and DNS | `trust`, `hosts sync`, `hosts clean` | [HTTPS](https://portless.sh/https), [Hosts](https://portless.sh/commands#hosts) | | Inspect and clean up | `list`, `doctor`, `prune`, `clean` | [Doctor](https://portless.sh/commands#doctor), [Prune orphans](https://portless.sh/commands#prune-orphans), [Clean up](https://portless.sh/commands#clean-up) | | Agents | `mcp` | [MCP server](https://portless.sh/commands#mcp-server) | Run `portless doctor` first when a URL does not load. It checks the proxy, routes, DNS, and CA trust without changing anything, and prints suggested fixes. ## Platforms portless runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows with Node.js 24 or later. `--tailscale` and `--funnel` need the Tailscale CLI, `--ngrok` needs the ngrok CLI, and `--cloudflare` needs `cloudflared`. ## Development This repo is a pnpm workspace with [Turborepo](https://turbo.build). The published package is `packages/portless/`, and the docs site is `apps/docs/`. Use Node.js 24 or later and pnpm 11: ```bash pnpm install pnpm build pnpm test pnpm lint pnpm type-check pnpm format ``` [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) lists the files to update with each change and the release process. ## Documentation - [portless.sh](https://portless.sh): getting started, commands, HTTPS, and configuration - [Why portless](https://portless.sh/why): the problems named URLs solve - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## License Apache-2.0

releases.name: v0.17.0
releases.body:
### New Features

- **HTTPS alias backends**: Added `--upstream` to `portless alias` to route an alias to an HTTPS or HTTP service on loopback. `--upstream https` enables TLS and keeps the incoming Host header. `--upstream https://<host>[:<port>]` also sets Host to that authority and sends a DNS hostname as SNI, and `http://<host>[:<port>]` sets Host without TLS. Upstream TLS supports HTTP/1.1 backends and does not verify the backend certificate. Restart the proxy after upgrading. (#568)
- **Worktree hostnames**: Added a `worktree` option to `portless.json` and the `package.json` `"portless"` key. `worktree.prefix: "branch"` uses the whole branch as the label, so `team-a/login` becomes `team-a-login`, and `worktree.hostnameTemplate` such as `tenant.{worktree}-{name}` replaces the whole hostname. Root values apply to every app in a workspace. Set the label directly with `portless run --prefix <label>` or `PORTLESS_PREFIX`, with `""` for none. Duplicate proxied hostnames fail before any app starts. (#548)
- **Alias TLD selection**: Added `--tld` to `portless alias` and `portless alias --remove` to cover only selected configured TLDs. Repeat the flag or pass a comma-separated list. A

releases.name: v0.16.0
releases.body:
### New Features

- **Docker Compose**: Added `portless compose` to run a Compose project with named URLs. Each published HTTP port moves to a fixed port on 127.0.0.1 and gets a `<service>.<project>.localhost` route, so two projects can publish the same host port. Database, cache, and UDP ports keep their published port. Configure services with the `portless.enable`, `portless.name`, and `portless.ports` labels. (#543, #547)

### Bug Fixes

- **Self-daemonizing commands**: Keep the route when a command starts a server in the background and exits, as Astro 7 does in agentic environments. The route moves to the server's PID, `portless list` shows it, and it drops once the server stops. (#444)
- **Upstream connections**: Pool connections to the dev server and limit concurrent dials per backend, so a cold HTTP/2 page load no longer overflows the server's accept backlog. Long-lived responses like SSE don't block other requests. (#477)
- **HTTP/2 request bodies**: Send HTTP/2 request bodies that have no `content-length` with chunked encoding, so GET, DELETE, and OPTIONS requests with a body no longer get a 400. (#478)

### Contributors

- @Railly
- @Umbranoxio
- @Tiancheng-Xu
- @ctate

releases.name: v0.15.13
releases.body:
### New Features

- **Unprivileged proxy mode**: Added `--unprivileged` and `PORTLESS_UNPRIVILEGED=1` to bind supported low ports without sudo, accept only loopback peers, and preserve the mode across restarts and service installation. (#529)

### Bug Fixes

- **Proxy privileges**: Check whether the requested listener needs root before asking for sudo. If elevation fails, stop with an error instead of silently switching ports. (#528)

### Documentation

- Added shared technical writing guidance for documentation changes. (#524)

### Contributors

- @Railly
- @ctate
- @bensabic

releases.name: v0.15.12
releases.body:
### New Features

- **MCP server**: Added `portless mcp` with tool profiles for route lookup, static aliases, proxy management, and diagnostics. (#513)
- **VitePress support**: Inject the assigned port and bind address for VitePress dev, serve, and preview commands. (#508)
- **Wrangler support**: Inject the assigned port and `--ip` bind address for `wrangler dev`. (#509)

### Bug Fixes

- **npm exec framework flags**: Pass injected framework options through `npm exec` and `npm x` after npm's option separator, while leaving ambiguous commands untouched. (#511)
- **Misdirected requests**: Return 421 for hostnames outside the configured TLDs instead of showing the app list, using HTML or JSON to match the client. (#512)
- **WSL-hosted containers**: Use the Linux trust store in containers that inherit a WSL2 kernel without Windows integration tools. (#507)

### Contributors

- @lahfir
- @ericclemmons
- @KennyMcSimpson
- @alistair3149
- @corvus-vardelabs
- @desilvakai
- @tlq5l

releases.name: v0.15.11
releases.body:
### Bug Fixes

- **Static aliases**: Allow `--force` to replace a static alias without treating it as a running process, and explain when the alias must be re-added. (#476)
- **Configuration source**: Report whether the configured app name came from `package.json` or `portless.json`. (#490)
- **Route liveness**: Keep live routes when the current user lacks permission to signal their processes. (#498)
- **Tailscale ports**: Account for ports held by foreground serve and funnel sessions when assigning HTTPS ports. (#499)
- **Astro global options**: Inject the assigned port and host when global options appear before the Astro subcommand. (#500)
- **Certificate scope**: Reject TLS server names outside the configured TLDs or with invalid hostname characters, and limit new macOS CA trust to SSL. (#497)
- **Certificate clock skew**: Backdate CA, server, and host certificates by five minutes on OpenSSL 3.4 or newer so clients with slightly slower clocks can connect. (#501)
- **Windows helper processes**: Hide console windows for OpenSSL and other helper commands when running without a terminal. (#502)

portless

Replace port numbers with stable, named .localhost URLs for local development. For humans and agents.

- "dev": "next dev"                  # http://localhost:3000
+ "dev": "portless run next dev"     # https://myapp.localhost

portless runs a local reverse proxy and gives each dev server a name. Your app listens on a free port that portless assigns, and you open https://<name>.localhost instead of remembering which port it took. The URL stays the same across restarts, so bookmarks, cookies, OAuth redirects, and an agent's test script keep pointing at the right app.

Install

npm install -g portless

To pin the version per project, install it as a dev dependency with npm install -D portless. portless is pre-1.0, so contributors may run different versions, and a change to the state directory format between releases can require running portless trust again.

Quick start

From a project with a "dev" script in package.json:

portless
# -> runs "dev", https://<project>.localhost

The name comes from package.json, the git root, or the directory. Pass a name and a command to choose both:

portless myapp next dev
# -> https://myapp.localhost
  • The proxy starts on the first run. It serves HTTPS with HTTP/2 on port 443, so the first run creates a local certificate authority, adds it to the system trust store, and may ask for sudo. Use --no-tls for plain HTTP, or --unprivileged to skip sudo (Unprivileged mode).
  • portless run <cmd> infers the name and detects git worktrees. In a linked worktree, the last / segment of the branch becomes a subdomain, so fix-ui.myapp.localhost and myapp.localhost run side by side. Use --prefix or PORTLESS_PREFIX to set the label, or configure the label style and hostname template.
  • A name with dots is a subdomain: portless api.myapp pnpm start serves https://api.myapp.localhost.
  • PORTLESS=0 pnpm dev runs the command directly, without the proxy.

The full walkthrough is in Getting started.

How it works

Each app gets a random port from 4000 to 4999 through the PORT environment variable, and registers a route from its hostname to that port. The proxy forwards https://<name>.localhost to the route. Most frameworks read PORT. For those that don't, such as Vite, Astro, Angular, Expo, and Wrangler, portless adds the matching port and host flags to the command (Port assignment).

Outside LAN mode, the proxy listens only on 127.0.0.1 and ::1. It keeps /etc/hosts in sync for route hostnames, which custom TLDs such as .test need. If a route hostname will not resolve, the command that registered it warns and points you to portless hosts sync.

To reach an app from another device or share it, use LAN mode for phones on the same network, or Tailscale, ngrok, or a Cloudflare quick tunnel with --tailscale, --ngrok, or --cloudflare.

Upstream aliases

Use --upstream to route an alias to an HTTP or HTTPS service listening on loopback:

portless alias api 8080 --upstream https
portless alias api 8080 --upstream https://api.internal
portless alias api 8080 --upstream http://api.internal

The positional port always dials loopback. https enables TLS and preserves the incoming Host header. An https:// authority enables TLS and overrides Host with the full authority, including its optional port. SNI uses a DNS hostname without the port; IP addresses are not sent as SNI. An http:// authority overrides Host without TLS. This setting does not change client-facing proxy TLS. Authorities accept only a hostname or IP address with an optional port, without credentials, paths, queries, fragments, or whitespace.

Upstream TLS connects only to an HTTP/1.1 backend on loopback. Portless disables certificate verification, so TLS does not authenticate backend identity, even through an SSH tunnel. Restart the proxy daemon after upgrading portless.

Configuration

An optional portless.json sets the name and script. In a monorepo, one file at the root covers every workspace package, and portless from the root starts all of them:

{
  "apps": {
    "apps/web": { "name": "myapp" },
    "apps/api": { "name": "api.myapp" }
  }
}

A "portless" key in package.json works too. Fields, precedence, Turborepo setup, and environment variables are in Configuration.

For AI agents

Install the portless skill into an agent harness from skills.sh:

npx skills add vercel-labs/portless

For MCP clients, portless mcp starts an MCP server over stdio. The default core profile lists routes, looks up URLs, and manages static aliases. --tools all adds proxy control and diagnostics:

{ "mcpServers": { "portless": { "command": "portless", "args": ["mcp"] } } }

The server does not start dev servers. Agents run portless run <cmd> in a shell. See MCP server.

Commands

Run portless --help for the full list, or portless <command> --help for one command.

Group Commands Docs
Run apps portless, run, <name> <cmd>, get Run an app, Get a service URL
Static routes alias, compose up, compose down Alias, Docker Compose
Proxy proxy start, proxy stop, service install, service status, service uninstall Proxy control, OS startup service
HTTPS and DNS trust, hosts sync, hosts clean HTTPS, Hosts
Inspect and clean up list, doctor, prune, clean Doctor, Prune orphans, Clean up
Agents mcp MCP server

Run portless doctor first when a URL does not load. It checks the proxy, routes, DNS, and CA trust without changing anything, and prints suggested fixes.

Platforms

portless runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows with Node.js 24 or later. --tailscale and --funnel need the Tailscale CLI, --ngrok needs the ngrok CLI, and --cloudflare needs cloudflared.

Development

This repo is a pnpm workspace with Turborepo. The published package is packages/portless/, and the docs site is apps/docs/. Use Node.js 24 or later and pnpm 11:

pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test
pnpm lint
pnpm type-check
pnpm format

AGENTS.md lists the files to update with each change and the release process.

Documentation

  • portless.sh: getting started, commands, HTTPS, and configuration
  • Why portless: the problems named URLs solve
  • Changelog

License

Apache-2.0

aiSummary.oneLiner: Portless provides secure, frictionless local development environments by automatically provisioning isolated URLs.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Portless eliminates the friction of managing local port conflicts by automatically assigning deterministic, human-readable URLs to local development servers. It operates as a background daemon that intercepts traffic and routes it dynamically to the appropriate underlying process. This allows developers to run multiple projects simultaneously without manually tracking which app is on which port. It provisions local TLS certificates automatically to ensure development environments mirror production security contexts. The tool streamlines team workflows by providing consistent local addresses across different machines.
keyFeatures: Automatic URL assignment: generates predictable, human-readable local addresses for development servers based on project names.
Dynamic traffic routing: intercepts local requests and forwards them to the correct process without manual port configuration.
Local TLS provisioning: automatically generates and trusts self-signed certificates to enable secure HTTPS connections locally.
Port conflict resolution: manages underlying port allocations invisibly so developers never encounter binding errors.
Daemon-based architecture: runs silently in the background to continuously monitor and map newly started development environments.

useCases.title: Multi-service local development
useCases.description: Run complex microservice architectures locally without needing to manually track and configure port assignments for each service.

useCases.title: Secure webhooks testing
useCases.description: Test third-party API integrations locally over HTTPS to ensure secure authentication flows function identically to production.

useCases.title: Standardized team onboarding
useCases.description: Provide new developers with consistent local URLs that match documentation perfectly regardless of their specific machine setup.

useCases.title: Frontend-backend integration
useCases.description: Develop separate frontend and backend repositories simultaneously while referencing them with clean local domain names.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Web developers and full-stack engineers managing multiple simultaneous local projects or microservices. It solves common pain points associated with local networking and certificate management.
